requirements.requirement: Join node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
requirements.summary: cmd-b202f72fbcb846d1 and cmd-eef6b0cee1504446 show node2 and node3 successfully joining node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster, with cluster_status confirming all three as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching RabbitMQ/Erlang versions.

requirements.requirement: Create a payments vhost with an application account that can publish and consume there
requirements.summary: cmd-208544fc80ae484e creates payments vhost with default-queue-type quorum and grants app_user full permissions; cmd-0745f8d7980248b9 creates app_user; cmd-a0687bbd5b314bb9 shows app_user declaring a queue via rabbitmqadmin; cmd-597ca9b0117a45f8 shows app_user publishing messages; cmd-a17ec9c7df934196 shows app_user consuming messages from a surviving node.

requirements.requirement: Durable queue is replicated across nodes for HA
requirements.summary: cmd-fa933f6e3c624bc7 shows the durable quorum queue 'orders' with members on all three nodes (rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3).

requirements.requirement: Messages published to the durable queue survive the loss of any one node and stay consumable from the remaining nodes
requirements.summary: cmd-225f3fe56ddc4084 confirms 3 durable messages present before disruption. cmd-e1db7b2963e24b1b stops node1 (the queue leader). cmd-f3dda17f8d8847c9 (observed from node2) shows only node2/node3 running yet the quorum queue re-elected a new leader (rabbit@node2) with all 3 messages intact; cmd-75eed19077a34f4a confirms queue state 'running' with 3 messages. cmd-a17ec9c7df934196 shows all 3 messages successfully retrieved from node2 while node1 was down, directly demonstrating the bounded disruption and consumability from a surviving node.

requirements.requirement: Cluster and queue recover fully after the disrupted node returns
requirements.summary: cmd-c7a4977b73504d4b restarts node1; cmd-ee7b032d30d84199 shows cluster_status with all 3 Running Nodes, no alarms/partitions, and the queue back to 3 members. cmd-d1a953da6a554c2f publishes fresh baseline messages confirming full functional recovery.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: a genuine 3-node RabbitMQ cluster was formed, a payments vhost with a fully functional app_user account was created, a durable quorum queue was replicated across all three nodes, and the key HA requirement was directly demonstrated (messages published, one node's leader stopped mid-run, quorum re-elected and messages remained consumable from a surviving node, then the node was restored with full recovery confirmed). The independent provider-wide node-restart protocol was also executed cleanly for all three nodes, each showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and full RabbitMQ/cluster/queue recovery, corroborated by the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene issues (leftover installer logs/scripts in /tmp, a broader-than-strictly-needed 'management' tag on app_user) are low-severity and do not affect task functionality.
limitations: The public task does not explicitly require the mandatory restart protocol, but it was executed and observed cleanly for all three nodes, so it does not lower functional confidence here.
Some benign repository-discovery failures (404s) occurred early in the trace but were read-only and did not affect final state; they are not counted as failures of the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace is largely clean and purposeful. Early failed discovery commands (404s probing wrong Cloudsmith/packagecloud repo paths for el10 erlang/rabbitmq packages, e.g. cmd-95c431ede09e42bb through cmd-2179ae371b534af8) were read-only diagnostics with no state mutation and directly led to the working el9-substitution fix, so they are not penalized. A vhost was deleted and recreated once (cmd-e6698a0bbd3b49d1 -> cmd-208544fc80ae484e) purely to add the missing --default-queue-type flag, a bounded corrective action with no lasting downside. A failed policy attempt (cmd-f4d735dcc58e4f6a) left no residue. The generated app_user password file (/root/app_pw.txt) was created with restrictive permissions and explicitly removed after use (cmd-0745f8d7980248b9), which is good practice. Two residual items remain: (1) numerous installer/log artifacts (/tmp/epel.log, /tmp/erl.log, /tmp/*_repo.log, /tmp/install*.log, /tmp/*.sh, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/cache.log, /tmp/start.log) were left in /tmp on all three nodes per the after_executor snapshot and were never cleaned up — low-risk but unnecessary residue; (2) app_user was granted the 'management' user tag (cmd-0745f8d7980248b9), which is broader than the minimum needed for AMQP publish/consume, though it was seemingly used to enable rabbitmqadmin/HTTP-API-based testing. Firewall changes opening RabbitMQ/clustering ports on all three nodes were necessary prerequisites for cluster formation and are not penalized.
